name: Taskly User Lifecycle
summary: The end-to-end experience of someone discovering, adopting, and becoming a regular user of the Taskly app — from first hearing about it through advocacy or churn.

stages.name: Discovery
actions: Sees an ad or hears about Taskly from a friend
thoughts: Another task app, is this one actually different?

emotions.label: Skeptical
emotions.description: Cautious — productivity apps have disappointed before, so the bar to even download is already high.

painPoints: App Store listing doesn't clearly differentiate from competitors
Screenshots look generic and don't show what makes Taskly unique
opportunities: Highlight unique features in first 3 screenshots
Add social proof (ratings, testimonials) to the App Store listing

stages.name: Download & First Open
actions: Taps install and waits for download
Opens the app for the first time
thoughts: Let me see what this can do.

emotions.label: Curious
emotions.description: Cautiously engaged — willing to give the app a chance but quick to abandon if the first screen is a wall of sign-up fields.

painPoints: Onboarding asks for account creation before showing the product
Loading time is noticeable on older devices
opportunities: Show the product before asking for sign-up
Progressive profiling instead of an upfront form

stages.name: Account Creation
thoughts: Why do they need all this information?

emotions.label: Mildly frustrated
emotions.description: Friction from the form dampens the initial curiosity. Social login expectations go unmet.

painPoints: Form requires full name, email, and password before seeing anything
No social login option (Google, Apple)
Email verification adds friction before any value is experienced
opportunities: Allow social login (Google, Apple)
Defer profile completion until after the first task
Skip email verification for the first 7 days

stages.name: First Task
actions: Views the completed task in the list

emotions.label: Engaged
emotions.description: Interested and exploring, but the blank slate is mildly intimidating without guidance.

painPoints: No guided tutorial or first-run walkthrough
Empty state is uninspiring and offers no starting point
Unclear how to set due dates or priorities
opportunities: Pre-populate with sample tasks to show what's possible
Contextual tooltips on first use of each feature
Quick-start template library

stages.name: Exploration
thoughts: Oh, it can do that too.

emotions.label: Pleasantly surprised
emotions.description: Discovering hidden depth creates genuine delight, but the discoverability of those features is too low.

painPoints: Advanced features are buried in menus and hard to find
No feature discovery prompts or in-app hints
Settings screen is overwhelming with no clear hierarchy
opportunities: Progressive feature reveals based on usage milestones
"Did you know?" nudges for underused features
Simplified settings with an Advanced toggle

stages.name: Habit Formation
thoughts: This is becoming part of my routine.

emotions.label: Satisfied
emotions.description: Routine is building. Users who reach this point are high-value, but many drop off before getting here because there's no external trigger.

painPoints: No reminders or push notifications enabled by default
No home screen widget available to glance at tasks
Daily digest email is too verbose to read quickly
opportunities: Smart default notifications (one morning reminder)
Launch a home screen widget for iOS and Android
Concise daily summary: 3 tasks, one-line format

stages.name: Power Usage
actions: Shares a list with a teammate or family member
Looks for calendar or tool integrations
thoughts: I need this to work with my other tools.

emotions.label: Committed but wanting more
emotions.description: Deep investment in the app but hitting a ceiling — missing integrations and collaboration features create frustration right when engagement is highest.

painPoints: No calendar integration (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar)
Sharing tasks with others is clunky and requires them to create an account
No support for recurring task patterns (e.g., every weekday)
opportunities: Google Calendar and Apple Calendar sync
Simplified sharing via link invite (no account required to view)
Smart recurring task suggestions based on past behaviour

stages.name: Advocacy or Churn
actions: Responds to an app review prompt (or ignores it)
Tells a friend about the app, or starts looking at alternatives
thoughts: Should I tell people about this or try something else?

emotions.label: Varies
emotions.description: Advocates are enthusiastic (5/5); churners are frustrated (1/5). The outcome here is shaped by everything that came before.

painPoints: No referral programme — there's no incentive to share
Support response time is slow, especially for free-tier users
Free tier limitations push users away before they experience full value
opportunities: Built-in referral rewards (e.g., one month of premium per referral)
Priority support response for users in their first 30 days
Extended premium trial to delay the paywall and build habit first

insights.text: Sign-up drop-off is 42% higher when the registration screen is the first thing users see vs. after a 3-screen product preview
7 of 10 usability test participants expected a 'Sign in with Google' option and expressed surprise when they couldn't find it
Users who create their first task within 5 minutes of sign-up have a 3× higher 30-day retention rate than those who don't
Only 12% of users discover the recurring tasks feature organically within their first month — the other 88% never use it
Push notification opt-in rate is 23% — but users who opt in have 2× the weekly active session count vs. those who don't
38% of churned users cited missing integrations (primarily calendar) as their primary reason for switching to a competitor
Users who refer at least one friend have an 89% 6-month retention rate vs. 41% for non-referrers — yet no referral mechanism exists in the app

changelog.description: Journey data published with full research findings, pain points, opportunities, and insights
